title: Classes and Objects
oneLiner: Defining a class, constructors versus __init__, methods, this versus self, C# properties versus Python attributes and @property, records and dataclasses, printing and comparing objects, and shared class data.
keyTakeaway: A class bundles data with the methods that work on it; each object built from it has its own copy of the data. Python makes the object explicit as self in every method; C# has an implicit this. Variables hold references to objects, so assigning one to another shares the object, and == on an ordinary class compares identity unless you use a C# record or a Python dataclass.
explanation:
So far, data and the code that works on it have lived apart: a list of readings here, a function to average them there. A class puts them together. It's a blueprint describing what data each thing has (a motor's name, rated speed and whether it's running) and what it can do (start, stop, describe itself). Each object, or instance, built from the class has its own copy of the data. This style of programming is called object-oriented programming, OOP.

A constructor is the special method that sets up a new object: a method named after the class in C#, called with new, and the method __init__ in Python. Methods are functions that belong to the class and work on one object, which they refer to as this in C# (usually implicit) and self in Python (always written out).

C# declares an object's data up front as typed properties, which can control who may read or change each value and can run checks when a value is set. Python objects get attributes simply by assigning to self.something, and use @property when a value needs checking or computing.

Objects live on the heap and variables hold references to them, so two variables can refer to the same object, and comparing two objects with == asks whether they are the same object unless the class says otherwise. C# records and Python dataclasses are short ways to write classes that are mainly data and compare by value. Inheritance and interfaces come later; OOP Basics in Software Design & OOP covers them in depth.
